findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_msg91_docs, get_msg91_api_docs, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Private data: get_msg91_api_docs, send_feedback_to_msg91, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Public sink: send_feedback_to_msg91, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Destructive: call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_msg91_docs, get_msg91_api_docs, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Private data: get_msg91_api_docs, send_feedback_to_msg91, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Public sink: send_feedback_to_msg91, call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91 · Destructive: call_any_read_api_of_msg91, call_any_api_of_msg91

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "call_any_read_api_of_msg91" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Read from any MSG91 API endpoint with a GET request for the user and return its response. Look up the exact endpoint with get_msg91_api_docs first (load the quickstart-msg91 skill for which tool to use when); never guess a URL. Pass the full url with path variables filled in and query params in `"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
